text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad belives that Malaysians were also involved in the recent speculative attacks on the ringgit by providing local currency to the raiders.
-- ASEAN and China are backing the review of UN human rights charter despite tough opposition from the U.S. and the European Union.
-- Tasek Cement was fined 90,000 ringgit ($34,615) for polluting the Kinta river in Malaysia's northern Perak state.
-- Chase Perdana is near finalising projects worth up to one billion ringgit in India, its executive chairman Mohan Swami said in the northern resort island of Langkawi.
-- The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange chairman Nik Mohamed Din said he was confident the share market will bounce back from months in the doldruns and the deserting foreign funds would also return.
-- The Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd (MIDF) was expected to start a broking unit by October, its chief executive Darwis Mohd Daek said.
